title: LRU with counters — predict the hit/miss ratio

aiGuide.intro: Small code, and then the real question: predict the hit ratio for different workloads **before** measuring. The prediction is what is scored — never let the AI make it.
plan: Ask: read-through? what counts as an eviction?
Fields: reuse your LRU; three counters; two tests
AI fills in GetOrLoad → review → run
Write your predictions down for four workloads
Run, compare prediction vs measurement, explain the gaps
Follow-ups: scan resistance, admission, LFU vs LRU

stages.name: LRU with counters
stages.yours: Decide what each counter means. **Read-through**: a miss calls the loader once and inserts. Hits, misses, evictions — and an eviction is counted only when an insert pushes an entry out.
stages.ai: **Co-generate** GetOrLoad. The LRU part is either yours already or a fields-pasted request like the LRU question.
bad: Add hit and miss counters to an LRU cache.
Counters in Get and Put separately: a Put of an existing key counts as a miss, the loader is never called, evictions are not counted.
No loader, so a miss costs nothing — the point of the metric is gone
good: Implement GetOrLoad(key, load) in CountingLruCache below. On a hit: hits++ and return the cached value without calling load. On a miss: misses++, call load once, insert, and if the insert evicted an entry, evictions++. Stats returns new CacheStats(hits, misses, evictions). Single-threaded. Keep my fields. List your assumptions first. Show only GetOrLoad and Stats.
States the edge: **a hit never calls load**
"Single-threaded" keeps it small; you will say what changes with threads
stages.reply: Typical defect: **evictions counted on every miss** once the cache has ever been full — or the loader called on a hit as well.
validate: A hit must not call the loader — count loader calls in the test
No eviction while filling; the first one at capacity + 1
HitRatio with zero requests is 0, not NaN
stages.fix: Counter placement is one or two lines → **by hand**.
stages.say: "A miss is a trip to the slow thing behind the cache, so that is what I count — and a hit must never call it."
stages.require: Implement `CountingLruCache<TKey,TValue>`: `GetOrLoad(key, load)` and `Stats`. An update is not an eviction.
stages.say_iv: Implement an LRU cache with counters: hits, misses and evictions. It is read-through — on a miss it loads from a slow source.

stages.name: Predict, then measure
stages.yours: **Write the predictions first**, in the pad as comments: a cyclic scan of capacity+1 keys → **0 hits**; the working set fits → only cold misses; uniform over N keys with capacity C → about **C/N**; Zipf-skewed → far better than uniform.
stages.ai: **Delegate the generators** (boilerplate) — never the prediction. Asking the AI "what will the hit ratio be" hands over the one thing being scored.
bad: Generate some workloads and tell me the hit ratio.
It runs the numbers and narrates them. You learn the answer instead of showing you knew it.
It made the prediction for you
"Some workloads" — not the ones that teach anything
No seed, so runs are not repeatable
good: Write three generators as IEnumerable<int>: Cyclic(distinct, length) = 0..distinct-1 repeated; Uniform(distinct, length, seed) using new Random(seed); Skewed(distinct, length, seed) where key k has weight 1/(k+1), using a running-sum array and binary search. And Run(capacity, keys) that feeds them through CountingLruCache. No analysis — I will predict first. Keep my CountingLruCache unchanged. State the complexity of each generator. Show only the generators and Run.
Names the efficient technique for Skewed
stages.reply: Typical defect: Skewed draws with a **linear scan over the weights** per sample (O(distinct) each — slow at 200,000 draws), or `new Random()` without the seed.
validate: Skewed: running sums + binary search, not a scan per draw
Cyclic with distinct = capacity: zero evictions
Prediction vs measurement — explain any gap out loud
stages.fix: A missing seed or a slow Skewed → **a one-line follow-up** naming the fix ("use new Random(seed)", "binary search the running sums").
stages.say: "LRU's worst case is a scan one bigger than the cache: every key is evicted just before it is needed. That is why databases add scan resistance."
stages.require: Add `static class Workloads` with `Cyclic(distinct, length)`, `Uniform(distinct, length, seed)`, `Skewed(distinct, length, seed)` (Zipf-like, s = 1) returning `IEnumerable<int>`, and `CacheStats Run(int capacity, IEnumerable<int> keys)`.
stages.say_iv: Before you run anything: if a client cycles through capacity-plus-one keys, what hit ratio do you expect? Then build a small simulator and check uniform and skewed workloads.

checklist: Which method, in which class — paste your class
Implement Log in the Logger class below
Every rule in one sentence, the boundary included
Keep my fields; no new public members
The wrong answers you expect, by name
No DateTime, no timers, no ConcurrentDictionary
Ask for assumptions first, or a reason per test
List your assumptions before the code
Keep the reply small enough to review
Show only Log · change only that line

none: You think and write. This is what is scored.
check: Ask it to attack your design or maths — no code.
cogen: Your design, pasted; the AI fills in mechanical code you can verify fast.
tests: Boilerplate you can check: ask for a reason per expected value.
review: A second reader for a named class of bug — "do not rewrite".
